heroHeadline: AUSSOM Configuration Plan Due UN Security Council as Egypt Deploys First Troops — 15 Days to Somalia's Presidential Legitimacy Cliff
heroSubtitle: April 30, 2026 marks the UNSC Resolution 2809 deadline for the African Union and the Federal Government of Somalia to submit updated AUSSOM configuration plans to the Security Council, as Somalia simultaneously welcomes Egypt's first AUSSOM contingent of approximately 1,100 troops — equipped with BAE Caiman MRAPs and NIMR Ajban APCs — as part of a bilateral defense pact partly motivated by Nile-state tensions with Ethiopia over the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. The configuration plan deadline arrives at a moment of maximum political pressure: with 15 days until President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's May 15 term expiry, Puntland warning the FGS 'will no longer be considered in existence' afterward, and no electoral roadmap agreed, Somalia's constitutional crisis is entering its final stretch. Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal in Hiiraan for an eleventh day as SNA/Macawisley counter-offensive efforts remain stalled. At sea, the Honour 25 fuel tanker with 17 multinational crew enters Day 6 of pirate captivity off the Puntland coast, with EU NAVFOR formally attributing the piracy resurgence — three vessels hijacked in one week — to the Iran War diverting coalition naval attention from counter-piracy operations. The International Maritime Bureau warned pirates will 'continue testing the waters.' Somalia's humanitarian catastrophe deepens: 6.5 million food insecure, 1.85 million children under five at acute malnutrition risk, and Iran-conflict Red Sea disruptions have raised humanitarian aid transport costs by 50% while the $852M response plan remains only 13.4% funded.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, OCHA, UNSOM, AFRICOM, EU EPF, EU NAVFOR, Combined Maritime Forces, UN Monitoring Group, and major international outlets. Casualty figures contested where noted.
